known.title: Isolate the developer’s Claude token from sandbox commands and app API keys

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Security. The new rule gives a sandbox run the developer’s `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, while the spec also runs repository code and injects sandbox secrets as environment variables for the run. Without a credential boundary, a repository test or Claude shell command can read and expose that personal token. Anthropic’s [environment documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars) says subprocess credential scrubbing requires an explicit setting. It also says `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` takes precedence in headless Claude runs: an app test that needs that key in the sandbox environment would silently bill the team’s key instead of using the developer’s subscription. The plan needs to define how model credentials are isolated from repository commands and app credentials.
findings.title: Isolate the developer’s Claude token from sandbox commands and app API keys

why: Claude rounds in Mainline sandboxes must use the developer's own Claude subscription, as the owner decided, with the team's API key only as the fallback
